correctness.rationale: Under u_{j+1}≥p_j+1, strictly increasing v_j, nonnegative masses h_t, each [u_j,v_j] total≥L>0 and tail [p_j+1,v_j]≤U≥0, let δ=L−U. When δ>0, at any index overlapped by r consecutive repair intervals each of r−2 interior precheckpoint portions [u_k,p_k] lies in the first tail and has mass≥δ; these pieces are disjoint, so (r−2)δ≤U and r≤2+floor(U/δ). Source gives explicit valid attaining examples for each ratio and arbitrarily large overlaps when L≤U, with distinct terminal endpoints. For consecutive separation p_{j+1}≤v_j implies next precheckpoint ≥L−U is contained in earlier tail≤U, hence L≤2U; legal two-repair counterexamples exist for L≤2U. Independently checked sample sharp constructions q=1,2,3 and boundary source L=4,U=1. At source constants L=S0,U=S0/4, strict separation implies nonconsecutive disjoint intervals, Σlength≤2n; Jensen and J≤B,n≤Bm give Σlog(n_j+1)≤B log(2m+1). Universal proof, not finite checks, establishes all L,U.
